blocks.text: Psalm 82 presents a poetic judgment scene: God stands in an assembly, addresses plural “gods” and “sons of the Most High,” condemns unjust judgment, and declares their mortality. Earlier Ugaritic writings also use scenes involving El and other divine figures in council, deliberation, messenger, and kingship settings. That comparison shows that assembly language existed in the region, but it does not make Ugaritic religion Israelite doctrine or settle the identity of the figures in Psalm 82. The psalm’s own language and message should therefore be read before treating a reconstructed divine-council system as the only possible explanation of every plural heavenly-being expression.
